issues.description: The solution's Lecture class declares attributes using snake_case names (e.g. lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students) but its constructor and methods reference camelCase names (e.g. lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents). This mismatch means the constructor assigns to non-existent fields (compile error) and deviates from the UML/description which uses camelCase attribute names. The template and problem statement expect camelCase attributes, but the solution's field names are inconsistent with both the UML and its own usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Align attribute names across artifacts: use the camelCase names shown in the UML and problem statement (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). In the solution file, rename the snake_case fields to the camelCase names (and keep them private) or update all usages (constructor and methods) to refer to the declared snake_case fields consistently. Ensure the template, solution, and UML use the same attribute identifiers so the constructor and methods compile and match the specification.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML) and the intended API use camelCase attribute names (e.g., lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). In the solution implementation the private fields are declared using snake_case (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) but the rest of the class (constructor, getters/setters, methods) refers to camelCase names (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, ...). This mismatch creates a naming inconsistency that breaks mapping between the UML/problem description and the code and will cause confusion (and compilation errors) for students trying to relate the specification to the implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent naming convention across artifacts. Rename the declared private fields in the solution to camelCase to match the UML and the rest of the class (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors), or alternatively change all usages to snake_case consistently. Also ensure the template's TODOs and example code expect the same camelCase names so students can directly map the problem statement to the code.
